newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel arms makers won't merge, govt official says.
newsitem.headline: Israel arms makers won't merge, govt official says.

text.p: The director general of Israel's defence ministry Ilan Biran has ruled out a merger of the country's five leading military manufacturers.

"The defence industries in Israel will not be merged despite the successful mergers of similiar industries in the United States and Europe," Biran said in an interview published in the Globes financial daily on Wednesday.

Directors of the five companies -- Israeli Aircraft Industries (IAI), Israel Military Industries (IMI), Rafael Israel Armaments Authority, Tadiran Ltd, and Elbit Systems Ltd, met last month to consider a privatisation and merger plan, according to a report this month in the Haaretz newspaper.
The plan, drafted by an external consultant, called for privatising government-owned IAI, IMI and Rafael and then merging them with private sector Elbit and Tadiran into one entity.

"We have no wish nor are we capable of subsidising their growth to an optimal level which would allow them to convert most of their production to export while maintaining the strategic production lines," said Biran.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed to privatise most government companies but military manufacturers are expected to be among the last because of security considerations.
Biran said he expected government-owned military industries to return to profitability next year after years of losses.
"The recovery will be completed by the middle of 1998," he told the newspaper.
